questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

The allegation was dismissed by the minister

options.text: The minister is dismissed the allegation
The minister had dismissed the allegation.
The minister has dismissed the allegation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 4'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **correct option** that expresses the given sentence in** active voice is 4)** The minister dismissed the allegation.
 
• The** given **sentence is in the** passive voice,** where the subject (the allegation) is receiving the action (dismissed) rather than performing the action.
 
• **To convert the sentence** to active voice, we need to make the subject (the minister) the doer of the action.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The minister dismissed the allegation.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1)** "The minister is dismissed the allegation" is** incorrect **because it is grammatically incorrect. The word order is incorrect, and the verb "dismissed" should be followed by the object, not preceded by it.
 
• **Option 2)** "The minister had dismissed the allegation" is** incorrect **because it uses the past perfect tense, indicating an action that occurred before another past action. It does not express the sentence in the active voice.
 
• **Option 3) **"The minister has dismissed the allegation" is** incorrect **because it uses the present perfect tense, indicating an action that started in the past and continues to the present. It does not express the sentence in the active voice.

• The** sentence states** that the speaker told someone their inner feelings, indicating a level of depth or intimacy.
 
• **To express** the **highest degree** of inner feelings, we use the superlative degree.

Therefore, the **correct answer **is: *'I told him my **innermost **feelings.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **original sentence** is in the** active voice**, with Fredrick as the subject performing the action of submitting the pending assignments.
 
• **To convert **it to **passive voice**, we need to make the pending assignments the subject of the sentence and indicate that they are receiving the action.

Therefore, the** correct sentence** is: *All the pending assignments had been submitted by Fredrick by Wednesday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2) **"All the pending assignments are to be submitted by Fredrick by Wednesday" is in the future passive voice, indicating that the assignments need to be submitted by a certain time.
 
• **Option 4)** "All the pending assignments are being submitted by Fredrick by Wednesday" is in the present continuous tense and does not reflect the past action mentioned in the original sentence.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

The thief asked if he remembered the place where they had hidden their jewellery.

options.text: The thief asked, “Where do you remember the place where we have hidden our jewellery?”
The thief asked, “Can you remember the place where we were hiding our jewellery?”
The thief asked, “Do you remember the place where we have hidden our jewellery?”
The thief asked, “Did you remember the place where we hid our jewellery?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 3".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The sentence** "The thief asked if he remembered the place where they had hidden their jewellery" is a** reported speech,** and the goal here is to **change it back **into direct speech.
 
• **When transforming** reported speech back into direct speech,** we need to change the tense back** to its original form.
 
• The verb **"remember" **remains the same as it's a mental verb which doesn't usually change in reported speech.
 
• In the original sentence,** "had hidden" **is in the **past perfect tense,** which usually transforms back into present perfect in direct speech, thus **"have hidden"** is the **correct tense **to use.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *The thief asked, “Do you remember the place where we have hidden our jewellery?”*

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Anne asked whether I knew a good lawyer.

options.text: Anne said, “Do you know a good lawyer?”
Anne asked, “Whether I knew a good lawyer?”
Anne said, ”You knew a good lawyer?”
Anne said, “Whether do you know a good lawyer?”

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Option 1".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **original sentence, **"Anne asked whether I knew a good lawyer,"** is in reported speech**. We have to transform it back into direct speech.
 
• Anne said, “Do you know a good lawyer?” - Here, the** 'knew'** (V2 form in reported speech) from the reported speech **returns to 'do you know**' (V1 form in direct speech).
 
• This is the **correct transformation** as it properly represents the reported sentence's meaning.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is: *Anne said, “Do you know a good lawyer?”*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's examine the **other options:**

 
 
• **Anne asked, “Whether I knew a good lawyer?” **- This is not correct because the word 'whether' is not used correctly in the question format in direct speech. 'Whether' is used in indirect or reported speech to indicate a question within a question.
 
• **Anne said, ”You knew a good lawyer?” -** This isn't correct because it isn't phrased as a question that expects an answer. It is a statement made in the form of a question which doesn't reflect the meaning of the original sentence correctly.
 
• **Anne said, “Whether do you know a good lawyer?” -** This option incorrectly uses 'whether' in a direct question. In direct questions, we don't use 'whether'; it's more appropriate in indirect or reported speech.
